solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unreasonable custom husband omitted a lot

indicators.note: omitted says a letter is left out of the word before it

parts.note: a custom is a habit, something regularly done
a lot means much, as in 'thanks a lot'

explanation.surface: A complaint that some practice, minus the husband, has been dropped a great deal: a domestic grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitted' takes H off HABIT, leaving ABIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is a bit much means it is excessive or unfair, so unreasonable.

clue.text: Stores right to break embargoes

indicators.note: to break into a word is to be put inside it, splitting it

parts.note: embargoes are prohibitions, or bans

explanation.surface: Shops are said to be breaking trade restrictions to do the right thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Barns are farm buildings used for storing hay and grain, so stores as a noun.

clue.text: It flows, steady at intervals

indicators.note: at intervals picks every other letter of the following word

parts.note: the letters of steady at even positions are picked; the reversed run across 'steady at' is a coincidence, not the setter's device

explanation.surface: Something said to flow steadily now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of steady. The Tay is Scotland's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a thing that flows, and the Tay is a Scottish river running past Perth and Dundee.

clue.text: Estuary, except the mouth, is brown

indicators.note: except the mouth means without its opening, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the Humber is a large estuary in north-east England

explanation.surface: A river estuary, all but where it meets the sea, is brown-coloured water.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'mouth' of a word is its first letter, which fits the estuary picture neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is an earthy pigment of brownish colour, used by painters.

clue.text: Army extremely eager to secure large place for gun

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it within, so the next letter goes inside

parts.note: a host is an army or great multitude

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme, outermost letters of the word eager

explanation.surface: A keen army wants a big position for its artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' as HOST is a crossword favourite, from the biblical 'host' of angels; 'extremely' gives the outside letters only.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is a leather case worn on the body to carry a pistol.

clue.text: City is in Pennsylvania? Yes and no

indicators.note: in says the word is goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: A question whether some city lies in Pennsylvania, answered with a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' is the setter's joke: the letters IS are in PA, but the Italian city is not in the American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisa is an Italian city in Tuscany, famous for its leaning tower.

clue.text: Scented mixture is up to prior to arrange

indicators.note: to arrange letters is to put them in a new order

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling blend that a monastery prior is responsible for arranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices kept for its fragrance.

clue.text: Able to pay as novel is damaged in street

indicators.note: in says the jumbled letters sit inside the abbreviation
damaged letters are broken up and put back in another order

explanation.surface: Someone can afford to buy because a book was spoiled out on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is damaged' signals the anagram of the book word; the result goes inside the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A solvent person or firm has enough money to meet all debts.

clue.text: Prime minister's dismal horse

definitions.meaning: Earl ... was a British prime minister, of 1832 Reform Act fame; 's stands for is
a dismal, gloomy day is a ... one
a horse with a white or greyish coat

explanation.surface: A political leader's sad old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: Earl Grey the Whig premier, the dull colour of gloom, and a pale-coated horse.

clue.text: Not develop much scorn

definitions.meaning: to stay small is, read as two words
to scorn someone here is to disparage or run them down

explanation.surface: Stunted growth earns contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle is to make someone seem unimportant, disparaging them; split, it reads as staying small.

clue.text: Make a request and invite trouble

definitions.meaning: behaviour that provokes a bad response, as in 'you were asking for it'

explanation.surface: Asking for something can provoke a bad reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means literally to request, and figuratively to provoke the punishment that follows.

clue.text: Precious little possibility of putting on weight

definitions.meaning: a scornful idiom for hardly any chance at all
literally a chance of getting fat

explanation.surface: There is hardly any likelihood of gaining pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means almost no prospect at all, while read literally it is the prospect of gaining girth.

clue.text: Welshman working we must interrupt

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the word we goes inside

parts.note: a machine that is working is switched on

explanation.surface: A man from Wales is busy, and we have to cut in on him.
explanation.definitionFit: Owen is a very common Welsh first name and surname, so a typical man of Wales.

clue.text: Grab tin at church

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: Seizing a tin can during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch is to seize something quickly and roughly, much the same as grabbing it.

clue.text: Regularly, west Scottish island turning up in recount

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters from bottom to top, backwards
regularly takes every other letter of the word west

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, off western Scotland

explanation.surface: An instruction for a recount, with a stray western Scottish island somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' gives ET from west; 'turning up' reverses ETARRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to tell it, the verb sense rather than counting votes again.

clue.text: Fish finger holds this for woman?

parts.note: her stands for a woman, the pronoun for a female person
a finger wears, or holds, a ring

explanation.surface: A puzzle over a fish finger and what it holds for a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish finger' looks like the food; split it, with Fish the definition and finger the start of a cryptic hint at a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The herring is a silvery sea fish, eaten fresh, smoked as kippers or pickled.

clue.text: I tarry in resort: that's not seen often

indicators.note: re-sorting letters puts them in a fresh order, read as re-sort

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker lingers at a resort, which seldom happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but is read as re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is an uncommon thing, something seldom encountered.

clue.text: Bow made of wood, initially pound off

indicators.note: initially says the letter goes from the front of the word
off says a letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: larch is a conifer and its timber
L stands for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An archer's bow made of timber, with the price knocked off first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' suggests the archer's weapon, but here it is a curved shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curve, and a bow can mean any curved, bent shape.

clue.text: Worthless blunder set in stone

indicators.note: set in says one piece is mounted inside another, like a gem in a ring

parts.note: a ruby is a precious stone
bish is British slang for a mistake or blunder

explanation.surface: A mistake that is carved in stone counts for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is informal British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rubbishy is trashy and of poor quality, so of little value.

clue.text: In public vehicle, go to return fake

indicators.note: In says the reversed word sits within the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is a public transport vehicle

indicators.note: to return is to come back, so the word go is read backwards

explanation.surface: Taking a bus back home turns out to be a sham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses the word go, and 'In' places the result within the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means counterfeit or not genuine, so false.

clue.text: CH2O2 processed into alcohol

indicators.note: processed means worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the chemical formula gives one C, two Hs and two Os

explanation.surface: A chemical formula, formic acid, refined into a spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the formula as letters: C, H, H, O, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooch is slang for crude or illicitly made spirits, so strong drink.

clue.text: Job for tradesman desperately keen to secure one

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast within, so the numeral is placed inside

parts.note: panting for something is longing for it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tradesman, desperate for work, holds on to a single job.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorating with brush and colour is work done by a decorator, a skilled trade.

clue.text: Native American bird

definitions.meaning: a Native American people of Montana
a black bird of the genus Corvus

explanation.surface: A bird native to the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a Plains nation of Montana and the large black corvid share the name.

clue.text: Cold greeting in foreign letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
hi is a casual greeting

explanation.surface: A frosty welcome is written in a letter from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests correspondence; here it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is the 22nd character of the Greek alphabet, so not one of ours.

clue.text: Used to be a sort of wolf?

definitions.meaning: past plural of the verb to be
the prefix that turns a wolf into a man-wolf of folklore

explanation.surface: A creature that was once something else, perhaps a kind of wolf.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the past plural of be, and also the prefix of the folkloric shape-shifting wolfman.

clue.text: Illumination breaking down halts gig

indicators.note: breaking down suggests a fault, so the letters fall apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A lighting failure brings a concert to a stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting supplied by burning coal gas in lamps, as in Victorian streets.
